_demand_record.unit: gross passenger boardings / one-way passenger-trips/year (Costa Verde 'Divisao Sul' system: Angra dos Reis + Mangaratiba + Abraao/Ilha Grande stations)
_demand_record.method: Arithmetic sum of the 12 published AGETRANSP 2023 monthly 'Divisao Sul' totals (Table 3.10). Same regulator/method as the four Rio lines. No doubling, halving, terminal allocation, or daily annualization.

_fare_record.source: AGETRANSP / CCR Barcas Costa Verde published tariff
_fare_record.method: Published R$20.50/leg (Angra<->Abraao) divided by BCB PTAX sell 5.0727 (2026-07-15). Passenger-facing benchmark only. Premium re-fare rule lifts this for premium-service planning.

_premium_substitute_fare_record.basis: Uber Black-equivalent premium water-taxi seat fare for the Angra<->Ilha Grande crossing. Navier serves the subsidized public ferry crossing only as a premium on-demand electric water-taxi, priced against the premium private fast-boat / premium ride alternative (private lancha transfers R$120-200/leg), never the subsidized public ferry.
_premium_substitute_fare_record.method: Angra-specific premium anchor. Private fast-boat transfer market R$120-200/leg corroborates a premium tier well above the R$20.50 public tariff; set to USD 30 planning benchmark. Not a claimed operator realized yield.
_premium_substitute_fare_record._decision: Jaideep explicit 2026-07-17: Angra-specific fare $30 (vs $28 Rio shared basis).

corridors._permission_status: No operating aquaviario line exists; system is at tender/EVTE stage awaiting federal licenses. Demand is a government pre-viability projection, not observed ridership. Not an operating authorization.

_demand_record.unit: projected one-way passenger-trips/year (transporte coletivo), daily-average annualized
_demand_record.source: https://www.sie.sc.gov.br/webdocs/sie/doc-tecnicos/aquaviario/ (EVTE Aquaviario RMF, Relatorio 3 - Componente Demanda; SIE-SC + BID)
_demand_record.method: Government pre-viability study (EVTE) projection. Base-year 2020 'Dia Util Medio' (average-working-day) route demand from Quadro 29, annualized using the study's OWN equivalent-working-days factor (Quadro 27: sum of monthly equivalent-working-days = 308/yr; weekends weighted Sat*0.50 / Sun*0.25-0.50). Tourism uplift (temporada) EXCLUDED = conservative. R3=12,633/day, R4=19,807/day (2020). PROJECTED demand for a PROPOSED, non-operating system; NOT observed boardings. Labeled as projection in deck; folded into SOM/TAM per Jaideep 2026-07-17 (underserved corridors we unlock).

_premium_substitute_fare_record.basis: Uber Black-equivalent premium ride-hail seat fare for the Florianopolis continent<->island crossing. Navier prices against the premium road alternative, never the proposed R$6.50 subsidized public catamaran tariff.
_premium_substitute_fare_record.method: Uber Black = 1.8x UberX (official Uber Brazil). Floripa cross-market UberX benchmark ~R$50-57 (e.g. FLN->centro R$57) -> Black ~R$90-103 -> /PTAX 5.0727 (2026-07-15) -> ~USD 18-20; set to USD 20 planning benchmark. Not a claimed operator realized yield.
_premium_substitute_fare_record._decision: Jaideep explicit 2026-07-17: Floripa priced on premium anchor estimate (Uber Black), NOT ferry/public transport tariff.

corridors._permission_status: Incumbent ferry-boat + lancha rapida system is state-concessioned (Internacional Travessias) and AGERBA-regulated. No transferable route-entry permission found. Treat as addressable passenger pool, not operating authorization.

_demand_record.unit: gross passenger crossings/year — COMBINED regulated Salvador–Itaparica system (ferry-boat São Joaquim–Bom Despacho + lancha rápida Salvador–Mar Grande)
_demand_record.source: Ministério do Turismo figures released at the Salvador–Itaparica bridge groundbreaking (2026-07-01), via Diário do Turismo 2026-07-03; Jan–May 2026 = 3.42M (~8.2M annualized run-rate) corroborates.
_demand_record.method: Official system total for calendar 2025 attached to the marquee São Joaquim–Bom Despacho crossing. COMBINED BASIS: includes the Salvador–Mar Grande lancha volume because AGERBA/Observatório publishes no per-mode annual split (Observatório PDF series unreachable 2026-07-19); the Mar Grande corridor is therefore carried at null demand to prevent double-counting. Salvador–Morro de São Paulo is ADDITIONAL to this series and is held separately.

_fare_record.unit: USD/pax/one-way comparable published public tariff (ferry-boat foot passenger, weekday)
_fare_record.source: AGERBA Resolução Nº 11 (2026-03-03) tariff table, in force 2026-03-06
_fare_record.method: Published R$7.20 weekday (R$9.50 weekend/holiday) divided by BCB PTAX sell 5.0727 (2026-07-15). Passenger-facing benchmark only; premium anchor below governs planning fare.
_fare_record.fx_source: BCB PTAX sell 2026-07-15 (locked for Brazil economics)

_premium_substitute_fare_record.basis: Premium bay-crossing anchor: schooner island day tours US$17.74–35.49 pp on the same waters; AGERBA's own 'Hora Marcada' +30% queue-skip tariff proves regulated premium willingness-to-pay; sits 6–10x above the US$1.42–2.60 commodity ferry/lancha floor and below live tour pricing.
_premium_substitute_fare_record.method: Approved batch anchor (handoff/partner-map-model/brazil-expansion-2026-07-19/FARE-ANCHORS-2026-07-19.md). Not a claimed operator realized yield.

corridors._permission_status: Crossing is state-run (Semil/DH), transitioning to the Acqua Vias PPP concession (Nov 2025 award; 100%-electric mandate). No transferable route-entry permission found. Addressable passenger pool only.

_demand_record.unit: modeled pedestrian+cyclist one-way crossings/year, São Sebastião–Ilhabela
_demand_record.source: Semil-SP official figures: H1-2024 system users 9,647,595 (8 litoral crossings); crossing share 15% of trips (Semil, Jul 2024); summer-operation mode split 593,073 ped+cyc of 1.15M users (15 Dec 2024–10 Mar 2025).
_demand_record.method: EXPLICIT MODEL, conservative: annual crossing users = 2 x H1-2024 implied (9,647,595 x 0.15 = 1,447,139) = 2,894,278 (low end of the record's ~2.9–4.0M/yr plausible range; January peak-season VDM deliberately NOT annualized). Addressable pool = pedestrians+cyclists only at the 51.6% summer-report mode share (593,073/1,150,000) = 1,493,447. Vehicle occupants excluded because a passenger water-taxi does not carry the car. No official per-crossing annual series exists (gap logged).

_fare_record.unit: USD comparable public benchmark (Aquabus single ticket ~US$3.94; Jan-2025 tourist-decree tariff ~US$9.86)
_fare_record.source: Prefeitura de Ilhabela Aquabus tariff + Jan-2025 decree
_fare_record.method: Public benchmarks only; premium anchor below governs planning fare.
_fare_record.fx_source: BCB PTAX sell 2026-07-15 (locked for Brazil economics)

_premium_substitute_fare_record.basis: State's own 'Hora Marcada' queue-skip tariff R$65.30–98/car = US$12.87–19.32 (3.4x standard — published willingness-to-pay on this exact crossing); Castelhanos private speedboats US$57–61 pp ceiling; R$48 vehicle-entry TPA fee favors passenger-first water mobility.
_premium_substitute_fare_record.method: Approved batch anchor (handoff/partner-map-model/brazil-expansion-2026-07-19/FARE-ANCHORS-2026-07-19.md). Not a claimed operator realized yield.

corridors.from: Terminal da Balsa Ponta da Praia (Santos)
corridors.to: Terminal da Balsa Guarujá (Av. Adhemar de Barros)
corridors._permission_status: Crossing is state-run (DH/Semil), transitioning to the Acqua Vias PPP concession (Nov 2025 award; pedestrian balsa free from 2026). No transferable route-entry permission found. Addressable passenger pool only.

_demand_record.source: Crossing-specific daily counts: ~7.6k pedestrians + ~7.7k cyclists = 15,300/day (Travessia Santos–Guarujá, A Tribuna basis, corroborated by DH system datasheets: system-wide 57k users/day across 8 crossings, Santos–Guarujá the busiest).
_demand_record.method: 15,300 ped+cyc/day x 365 = 5,584,500/yr. Year-round 24/7 commuter crossing (not seasonal), so calendar annualization is appropriate; vehicles (21k/day) excluded — water-taxi addresses foot/cycle passengers. No open per-crossing official annual series (gap logged; DH data-room request recommended). POSITIONING NOTE: pedestrian balsa is fare-free from 2026 — Navier sells the premium lane (speed/comfort/marina), never fare-vs-balsa.

_fare_record.source: Acqua Vias PPP terms / state announcement
_fare_record.method: Incumbent pedestrian crossing is free; premium anchor below governs planning fare.
_fare_record.fx_source: BCB PTAX sell 2026-07-15 (locked for Brazil economics)

_premium_substitute_fare_record.basis: Uber's published tier ladder for the Guarujá→Santos road detour (Uber route page, Jul 2026): UberX R$44=US$8.67, Comfort R$52=US$10.25, Bag R$63=US$12.42 (top listed passenger tier; Uber Black not offered on this corridor). $12 = top-of-ladder equivalent.
_premium_substitute_fare_record.method: Approved batch anchor, revised $10→$12 (handoff/partner-map-model/brazil-expansion-2026-07-19/FARE-ANCHORS-2026-07-19.md, PR #297). Not a claimed operator realized yield.

_demand_record.source: SEMOBI official: 'Aquaviário comemora um ano de atividade com marca de 500 mil passageiros'; corroborated by SEP Mar-2026 (>1.2M cumulative through Dec 2025 ⇒ ~500–550k/yr run-rate).

corridors.to: Ilha do Mel — Trapiche de Nova Brasília
corridors._permission_status: Pontal do Sul ↔ Nova Brasília/Encantadas crossing is AGEPAR tariff-regulated (Abaline operators); Paranaguá services are authorized boats outside the tariff table. Car-free island — boats are the only access. Addressable passenger pool only.

L3_locals.pool_basis: gross (boardings toward the island, all origins; direction split unavailable — conservative)

_demand_record.unit: passenger boardings embarked for Ilha do Mel, calendar 2025, all origins (Pontal do Sul + Paranaguá)
_demand_record.source: Abaline (official crossing operators' association) via Gazeta do Povo; corroborated by IAT park visitation 247,020 (2025, most-visited state park in Paraná; +21% vs 2024).
_demand_record.method: Operator-association annual figure used as-is. CONSERVATIVE: the figure is not broken down by direction (gap logged); if it counts outbound only, true one-way legs ≈ 2x (every visitor returns by boat — the island has no road access). Return legs deliberately NOT added. New Imply electronic ticketing (contracted Dec 2025) will produce exact regulator-grade counts — refresh then. Attached to the AGEPAR-regulated Pontal do Sul–Nova Brasília corridor; Encantadas leg held at null to prevent double-counting.

_fare_record.unit: USD/pax/one-way equivalent of AGEPAR-homologated round-trip tariff (R$44.77 RT, Mar-2023 values; 2025/26 market one-way ~US$9.66)
_fare_record.source: AGEPAR homologated tariff table (Mar 2023); 2025/26 season market pricing
_fare_record.method: Homologated R$44.77 RT / 2 / PTAX 5.0727. Newer tariff table not yet located (gap logged); premium anchor below governs.
_fare_record.fx_source: BCB PTAX sell 2026-07-15 (locked for Brazil economics)

_premium_substitute_fare_record.basis: Market one-way already ~US$9.66 (2025/26 season); AGEPAR-homologated nautical-taxi premium tier R$69.07 RT = US$13.62 proves a regulated premium tier exists. $12/leg is a modest premium over the market one-way for a faster, cleaner, bookable service. No ride-hail comparator exists on a car-free island — the regulated premium tier is the ceiling evidence.
_premium_substitute_fare_record.method: Approved batch anchor (handoff/partner-map-model/brazil-expansion-2026-07-19/FARE-ANCHORS-2026-07-19.md). Not a claimed operator realized yield.
